subject: RE: DPA negotiation - breach notification, subprocessors, and transfer terms (Acme Payments)
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acme-payments.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Bradley <t.bradley@acme-payments.com>, legal+contracts@acme-payments.com
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:31:00 -0500
Subject: Initial DPA redlines and question on breach timelines

Hi Mina —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We're ready to move forward but our legal team has a few standard redlines to the DPA and one key question around breach notification timing. Attached is our redlined DPA (DPA-Acme-Redlines.docx). High-level asks: 

- Breach notification: our standard is "as soon as reasonably practicable, but no later than 24 hours for confirmed incidents affecting personal data". Can Redwood accept 24 hours?
- Subprocessors: we require 30 days prior notice of new subprocessors and the right to object.
- Data transfers: we typically require SCCs and a statement of transfer mechanisms.

Could you confirm whether Redwood can (1) commit to 24-hour notification, (2) provide a current subprocessor list, and (3) confirm SCCs or equivalent? We can turn around counters quickly if needed.

Appreciate it —
Elena Rossi
Head of Legal Operations
Acme Payments

Attachment: DPA-Acme-Redlines.docx (Word document containing track changes)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 10:02:00 -0500
Subject: RE: Initial DPA redlines and question on breach timelines

Hi Elena —

Thanks for sending — we appreciate the clear asks. I'm looping in Redwood legal (cc'd) and your AE so we can get this over the finish line quickly. Initial responses:

- Breach notification: we aim for prompt notifications and have operational SLAs; legal will propose concrete language (timing + severity carveouts).
- Subprocessors: we can provide a current list and propose 30 days' notice for additions; we have standard objection language.
- Transfers: Redwood uses SCCs for EU transfers and a transfer addendum for other jurisdictions.

Neha (legal) — can you review Elena's redlines and propose Redwood's counterpoints? Marissa/Aditya — please confirm commercial tolerance for any timing concessions.

Best,
Mina Haddad
VP, Customer Success (acting as primary contact for this account)
Redwood Inference

Note: I'm available for a 20-min call if Elena prefers to walk through the redlines live.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 11:15:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood proposed DPA counter (highlights)

Team —

I've reviewed Acme's redlines and drafted an initial response attached (Redwood_DPA_Response_v1.docx). Summarized negotiation positions below (legal highlights):

1) Breach notification timing
   - Acme: 24 hours for confirmed incidents.
   - Redwood: we can commit to "initial notification within 72 hours of confirming unauthorized access affecting personal data" with an intermediate requirement to notify sooner for critical incidents where feasible. Proposal: "Company will notify Customer of any confirmed security incident affecting Customer personal data as soon as reasonably practicable and, in any event, no later than seventy-two (72) hours after Redwood confirms the incident; for incidents classified as "Critical" (unauthorized exfiltration or confirmed access to production data), Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to notify within twenty-four (24) hours of confirmation."

   Rationale: 24 hours is operationally tight for confirmation and investigation across regions; the proposed two-tiered approach balances Acme's need for speed and our need to avoid false positives.

2) Subprocessors
   - We will provide the current subprocessor list (attached CSV) and will notify customers of additions at least 30 days in advance. We keep a standard objection right and will evaluate objections in good faith.

3) Data transfers
   - Redwood uses EU SCCs for EEA transfers and provides a transfer addendum. We'll confirm on any other cross-border mechanisms for APAC customers; for Acme (US/EU footprint) SCCs + contractual addendum should satisfy.

4) Incident cooperation and investigations
   - We propose defined cooperation steps, timelines for evidence preservation, and a root cause analysis deliverable within 30 days of incident confirmation (subject to operational constraints).

5) Execution
   - We prefer DocuSign for signature. I'll prepare the executed-ready DPA once commercial terms are agreed.

I've attached: Redwood_DPA_Response_v1.docx and subprocessor_list_20260220.csv. Comments welcome; I can incorporate tweaks before we share the counter with Acme.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Response_v1.docx; subprocessor_list_20260220.csv

From: Tom Bradley <t.bradley@acme-payments.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acme-payments.com>, legal+contracts@acme-payments.com
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 08:12:00 -0500
Subject: RE: Redwood proposed DPA counter (highlights)

Neha —

Thanks for the thoughtful response. Two quick points from Acme Legal: 

1) We appreciate the two-tier approach but remain focused on an enforceable 24-hour clause for confirmed incidents that materially affect payment data. 72 hours is acceptable only for low-risk or confirmed non-payment data incidents. Can Redwood agree to a scope-limited 24-hour timeline for incidents impacting payment card or personally identifiable payment data?

2) Execution: Acme prefers to have the final DPA returned via DocuSign within 3 business days after counters are agreed. Please send a DocuSign envelope when ready.

We attached a short PDF with our requested amendment snippets (Acme_Requested_Amendments.pdf).

Tom Bradley
Head of Partnerships
Acme Payments

Attachment: Acme_Requested_Amendments.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Bradley <t.bradley@acme-payments.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 14:36:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Redwood proposed DPA counter (highlights)

Tom/Elena —

Thanks for the pragmatic feedback. Commercially, Redwood can accept a narrower 24-hour obligation limited to "confirmed incidents that materially impact payment or financial data (including cardholder data and authenticated payment credentials)." For other categories of personal data, we request the 72-hour initial notification with the Critical/24-hour carveout Neha proposed.

Other confirmations: 
- Subprocessors: we'll publish the current list and provide 30 days' prior notice for any additions; your team may raise objections during the notice period as per the DPA.
- Transfers: we will include the EU SCCs and a transfer addendum; we will provide a statement of transfer mechanisms in the executed DPA.

Next steps: Neha will update the DPA language; once Acme signs off on the final redlines, we'll send a DocuSign envelope and ask for signature within 3 business days. Proposed compromise bullet for breach notification to be included in the DPA text: 

   "For incidents involving payment or financial data as defined in Appendix A, Company shall use commercially reasonable efforts to notify Customer within twenty-four (24) hours of confirmation. For all other personal data incidents, Redwood will notify Customer as soon as reasonably practicable and, in any event, no later than seventy-two (72) hours after confirmation; Redwood will provide updates as investigation proceeds."

Link to DocuSign (placeholder): https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123456789

Happy to hop on a 15-min call to greenlight wording.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

PS: Aditya — please confirm that a 24-hour carveout limited to payment/financial data is acceptable commercially.

Attachment: (none in this message)

Once we have the countersigned DPA we can finalize provisioning. Looking forward to going live.

Elena Rossi
